page: Amazon Web Services c6g.xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine running on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by custom AWS Graviton2 processors utilizing the 64-bit ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 microarchitecture. The instance features 4 physical cores, mapping to 4 dedicated vCPUs with a single thread per core operating at 2.5 GHz. The CPU memory cache structure consists of 64 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and a shared 32 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity is configured at 8.0 GB, providing a standard compute-optimized ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware cryptographic acceleration includes support for AES instructions.

The instance does not include integrated GPUs or local NVMe storage, relying solely on network-attached storage architectures. Baseline network bandwidth is rated at 1 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned by default.

Benchmark outcomes show varied performance characteristics across workloads. Single-core processing in stress-ng registers in the middle tier at 1519.79, while multi-core stress-ng records 6053.66, falling in the lower 25% bracket. Synthetic testing via Geekbench yields a single-core score of 965.0 and a multi-core score of 3252.0. Large-block memory bandwidth shows consistent mid-tier results, reaching 71.99 GB/sec for uncached read operations and 35.14 GB/sec for writes. PassMark metrics reflect constraints in encryption performance (543.57) and overall CPU score (2702.45), while database operations register solidly in the middle 50% at 2589.21. In-memory tasks through Redis demonstrate 4.76 million SET operations per second, and static web serving achieves 4.95 GB/sec.

Cost efficiency is driven by the power-efficient Arm architecture, delivering stable core isolation without simultaneous multithreading interference. However, lack of advanced vector instruction sets like AVX-512 or AMX and the modest 1 Gbps network baseline restrict throughput in vector-heavy computation and distributed transfers. Workload fit includes medium-load web serving, containerized services, microservice backends, CI/CD compilation, and lightweight database applications that are natively compiled for arm64.
description: Amazon Web Services c6g.xlarge is a compute-optimized instance driven by custom 64-bit ARMv8 AWS Graviton2 Neoverse-N1 processors running on the Nitro hypervisor. The virtual machine delivers 4 dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading, running at 2.5 GHz alongside 8.0 GB of memory (2.0 GB per vCPU). The system provides 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, contains no local storage, and includes no GPU accelerators. In benchmarks, it exhibits mid-tier performance for uncached large-block memory read and write bandwidths as well as PassMark database operations, but registers lower throughput in heavy vector arithmetic and multi-core computational tests. Featuring hardware-accelerated AES instructions and physical core predictability, c6g.xlarge is suited for arm64-native applications such as web servers, microservices, continuous integration pipelines, and light caching tiers.
